numerical_failure.observed_behavior: When adding/subtracting a timedelta64 ndarray to/from a Timedelta, out-of-bounds results were silently wrapped/landed on the NaT sentinel and returned as NaT (missing) or wrapped values instead of raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Raise :class:`OutOfBoundsTimedelta` for out-of-bounds sums, and reject a sum landing exactly on the NaT sentinel instead of returning NaT—matching the scalar :class:`Timedelta`/TimedeltaIndex behavior.
trigger_conditions: Out-of-bounds sum: result silently wrapped or saturated instead of raising
Sum landing exactly on the iNaT sentinel coming back as NaT/missing instead of raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta
Unit promotion wrap: promotion to the finer of the two units wrapped (e.g., s->ns)

oracle_clues: whatsnew notes: previously an out-of-bounds ndarray result silently wrapped; result landing exactly on the NaT sentinel came back as missing instead of raising OutOfBoundsTimedelta (:issue:`66552`)
commit notes: Timedelta added/subtracted with timedelta64 ndarray silently wrapped; promotion to finer unit wrapped; sum landing exactly on iNaT returned NaT
code change: route operations through add_overflowsafe/astype_overflowsafe so casting and addition raise instead of wrapping; iNaT sentinel is rejected rather than passed off as missing

numerical_characteristics.magnitude: stepping one unit past the bottom of the range (i.e., operations involving Timedelta(np.timedelta64(-(2**63)+1, unit)) and adding/subtracting one of dtype m8[{unit}]); also out-of-bounds sums at/just beyond int64 limits
category_specific_evidence: Timedelta added to a timedelta64 ndarray previously handed the operation to numpy, so an out-of-bounds sum silently wrapped, the promotion to the finer of the two units wrapped, and a sum landing exactly on iNaT came back as NaT; route through add_overflowsafe/astype_overflowsafe so these cases raise instead of wrapping/NaT (GH#66552).
Reproducer: `Timedelta.min + np.array([-1], "m8[ns]")` -> `array(["NaT"], dtype="timedelta64[ns]")` with comment: sum fits in int64 but *is* iNaT.
Reproducer: `Timedelta.min + np.array([-2], "m8[ns]")` -> `array([9223372036854775807], dtype="timedelta64[ns]")` with comment: wrapped past int64.
Reproducer: `Timedelta(10**12, "s") + np.array([1], "m8[ns]")` -> `array([3875820019684212737], dtype="timedelta64[ns]")` with comment: wrapped on the s -> ns promotion.

Mathematical/semantic property violated: an out-of-bounds addition/subtraction should raise OutOfBoundsTimedelta rather than (a) wrap in int64, and (b) convert a sum landing exactly on the NaT/iNaT sentinel into returned NaT (instead of raising), matching scalar Timedelta/TimedeltaIndex behavior (GH#66552).

Test requirement: `td_min = Timedelta(np.timedelta64(-(2**63) + 1, unit))` and `one = np.array([1], dtype=f"m8[{unit}]")`; then `td_min - one`, `td_min + (-one)`, and `(-one) + td_min` must raise `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` with message `Out of bounds {attrname} timedelta` (stepping one unit past the bottom of the range lands on iNaT and must raise).

Unit handling aside: for year/month units, Timedelta(1, "ns") + np.array([1], dtype="m8[Y"]) and similarly for "M" must raise TypeError with message `Cannot get a common metadata divisor` (relevant to reproduction setup for freq in {"Y","M"}).
reproduction_risks: Must set up inputs with the exact dtype/unit behavior shown: use `Timedelta.min` with a `np.array(..., "m8[ns]")` containing -1 or -2 to demonstrate NaT/iNaT handling and int64 wrapping; using different units or values may not hit the iNaT sentinel or overflow boundary.
For the second wrapping case, use `Timedelta(10**12, "s")` together with `np.array([1], "m8[ns]")` to ensure the s -> ns promotion path wraps as shown.

If reproducing via the unit-parametrized test, the out-of-bounds threshold must be `Timedelta(np.timedelta64(-(2**63) + 1, unit))` and the step must be exactly `one = np.array([1], dtype=f"m8[{unit}]")` (or its negation) to land on iNaT and trigger OutOfBoundsTimedelta rather than returning NaT.
